mainTopic: When the ban on eating on ערב פסח begins, and which snacks and drinks are still allowed
overview: The משנה says that on ערב פסח, close to מנחה, a person may not eat until dark. The גמרא asks which time is meant. Close to מנחה גדולה would be because of the קרבן פסח. Close to מנחה קטנה would be so that he eats the מצה with appetite. רבינא proves from a ברייתא about King אגריפס that the משנה means מנחה קטנה. The גמרא challenges the proof, then answers that the ברייתא teaches that even אגריפס, with his late mealtime, is bound by the ban. Next, a sage rules that light snacks are still allowed. This is supported by רבי יצחק's practice, by a ברייתא about a waiter serving intestines to the guests, and by a hint from a פסוק in ירמיה. Finally, רבא drank wine all day on ערב פסח to build his appetite for מצה. He begins to bring a משנה as proof that wine whets the appetite, and that משנה is quoted on the next עמוד.

steps.title: First option ends: the worry is about the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the first side of its question. If the משנה means close to מנחה גדולה, the worry is that a person will get caught up in his meal and not bring the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he will end up holding back from bringing the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that began on the previous דף. The question is whether the משנה's ban means close to מנחה גדולה because of the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה גדולה is about half an hour after midday, which is around when the קרבן פסח could start being brought. If the ban starts that early, the reason must be the offering: a person who sits down to a meal may get absorbed in it and miss bringing his פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: the earliest מנחה time, about 6.5 hours into the day

steps.confusionAlert: This is the middle of a sentence that started on the previous דף. The first half asked: 'Did we learn close to מנחה גדולה, and the reason is that he might get drawn into his meal…'

phrases.english: and he will come to refrain from performing the Pesach offering.
phrases.notes: End of the first side of the question, which began on 107a.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which time does 'סמוך למנחה' in the משנה refer to, and what is the reason for the ban?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question begun on the previous daf.

steps.title: Second option: the worry is about eating מצה with appetite
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the משנה means close to מנחה קטנה. Then the reason is מצה: if he eats late in the day, he will eat the מצה at night with no appetite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה', and the reason is because of מצה: perhaps he will come to eat the מצה as overstuffed eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question. Maybe the ban starts only near מנחה קטנה, late in the afternoon, so that he will still be hungry for the מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two options give two different times and two different reasons. Under the second option, the ban only starts about 9.5 hours into the day. The concern is the quality of the מצוה at night: eating מצה when already full is אכילה גסה, which is not a proper way to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
the later מנחה time, about 9.5 hours into the day
overstuffed eating, forcing food down without appetite

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, סָמוּךְ לְמִנְחָה קְטַנָּה תְּנַן —
phrases.english: Or perhaps we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה'
phrases.notes: Second option for reading the משנה.

phrases.english: and the reason is because of matza:
perhaps he will come to eat the matza
as overstuffed eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, סָמוּךְ לְמִנְחָה קְטַנָּה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ban close to מנחה קטנה, for the sake of eating מצה with appetite?

steps.title: רבינא brings the case of King אגריפס
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a ברייתא. Even King אגריפס, who normally ate at nine hours, did not eat on ערב פסח until dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear: Even King אגריפס, who usually eats at nine hours, on that day may not eat until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a source to answer the question. This step just quotes the ברייתא; the next steps explain how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine hours is about three hours before sunset, which is late for a meal. The ברייתא uses the word 'even' (אפילו), which tells us there is something special about אגריפס holding back. רבינא will use that word as his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: nine hours into the day (about three hours before sunset)

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
Even King Agrippa,
who is accustomed to eat at nine hours,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ.
phrases.english: on that day he may not eat until it gets dark.

steps.raayaObject: That the משנה means close to מנחה קטנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about King אגריפס, who ate at nine hours

steps.title: Under the מנחה קטנה reading, אגריפס's restraint is special
steps.stepSummary: If the ban starts close to מנחה קטנה, then nine hours is still allowed. So it is a real praise that אגריפס held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה': that is the special greatness of אגריפס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that the ברייתא fits the מנחה קטנה reading. אגריפס gave up a meal he was technically still allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine hours comes before the ban near 9.5 hours begins. So when אגריפס skipped his usual meal, he went beyond what was required. That is why the ברייתא says 'even אגריפס'.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well if you say
his special greatness; the novelty in his case

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה',
that is the greatness of Agrippa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא סָמוּךְ לְמִנְחָה קְטַנָּה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ברייתא fits the second option.
steps.raayaObject: That the מנחה קטנה reading explains the word 'even' in the ברייתא

steps.title: Under the מנחה גדולה reading, there is nothing special
steps.stepSummary: If the ban starts close to מנחה גדולה, then at nine hours eating was already forbidden for everyone. So there is no special praise for אגריפס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say we learned 'close to the greater מנחה', what is the greatness of אגריפס? The ban already fell on him from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that the other reading does not fit the ברייתא. Under that reading, אגריפס did nothing special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating is banned from about 6.5 hours, then by nine hours everyone is already forbidden to eat. אגריפס simply obeyed the law like everyone else, so the word 'even' would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: but if you say (introduces the reading that fails)

phrases.english: But if you say
we learned 'close to the greater מנחה',
what is the greatness of Agrippa?
The prohibition already took effect on him from the outset!
phrases.notes: It began right after midday, well before nine hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ סָמוּךְ לְמִנְחָה גְּדוֹלָה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other half of the בשלמא structure: this reading fails the test.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'even' in the ברייתא would make no sense under that reading

steps.title: Conclusion: the משנה means close to מנחה קטנה
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה must mean close to מנחה קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא concludes his proof. The ban starts near מנחה קטנה, and its reason is to keep an appetite for the מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one reading lets the ברייתא's praise of אגריפס make sense, so that reading wins. This answers the opening question in favor of the second option.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא's proof, the ban on eating on ערב פסח starts close to מנחה קטנה (about 9.5 hours into the day), so that the מצה will be eaten with appetite.

phrases.english: Rather, we learned 'close to the lesser מנחה'.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה refers to close to מנחה קטנה.

steps.title: Challenge: אגריפס's meal would reach the forbidden time anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even under the מנחה קטנה reading, what was special about אגריפס? His meal would still run into the time of the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, what is the greatness of אגריפס? The time of the prohibition was reaching him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's proof. Even under the reading he chose, אגריפס seems to have done nothing extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A meal started at nine hours would last past the start of the ban near 9.5 hours. So starting it was already forbidden, and holding back was just following the law. That weakens the proof from the word 'even'.

keyTerms.meaning: was reaching him / had arrived for him

phrases.english: Ultimately, what is the greatness of Agrippa?
The time of the prohibition was arriving for him!
phrases.notes: His meal would extend into the forbidden time.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the מנחה קטנה reading explains אגריפס's greatness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nine hours is so close to the ban that his meal would be forbidden anyway, so there is still no special praise.

steps.title: Answer: we might have thought אגריפס's late schedule makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's point is that אגריפס is not an exception. We might have thought that his nine-hour meal counts like a normal person's four-hour meal, but it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that nine hours for אגריפס is like four hours for us. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The 'even' in the ברייתא does not mean אגריפס went beyond the law. It means the law applies even to someone with his unusual schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אגריפס always ate his first meal late, so his nine hours worked like an ordinary person's four-hour breakfast. We might have thought he was allowed to keep his usual meal time. The ברייתא teaches that the ban follows the clock, not a person's personal schedule, so the proof for the מנחה קטנה reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
it teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer means אגריפס did something beyond the law. The new point is only that his late schedule does not exempt him; the ban applies to him like everyone else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבינא's proof standing: the ban on eating starts near מנחה קטנה. It also teaches that the ban follows the actual hour of the day, not a person's personal eating habits.

phrases.english: Lest you say
nine hours for Agrippa
is like four hours for us,
phrases.notes: Four hours is the normal mealtime for ordinary people.

phrases.english: it teaches us that it is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא תֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת לְאַגְרִיפַּס כְּאַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת דִּידַן דָּמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the novelty of the ברייתא: it is about including אגריפס in the ban, not praising him for going beyond it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because his normal mealtime was so late, his nine hours might count like an ordinary four hours, so he could keep his usual meal.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no special exception for אגריפס; the ban follows the clock for everyone, and the proof for מנחה קטנה stands.

steps.title: Light snacks are still allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי (יוסי) rules that even during the ban, one may dip and eat light snack foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי (יוסי) said: But a person may dip and eat light snack foods.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage adds a limit to the ban on eating before פסח night. A real meal is forbidden, but light snacks are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is about not filling your stomach before the סדר. Snack foods like fruit or small bits of meat do not fill you up. So they do not go against the reason for the ban. The word אבל ('but') shows this is an exception to the ban we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: dips (food into a sauce or dip) and eats it
kinds of snack foods, like dessert or light refreshments, not a full meal
but; here it marks an exception to the ban

steps.confusionAlert: The name in parentheses (יוסי) shows the text is unsure about the exact name of the sage. Do not let this distract you. The point is the rule: snacks are allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Yosei) said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name יוסי here and some don't, so we can't be sure which רבי said this.

phrases.english: but he may dip and eat
phrases.notes: An exception to the ban on eating close to מנחה.

phrases.english: kinds of snack foods.
phrases.notes: Light foods that do not make a full meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ban's start time is set (close to מנחה קטנה), this step shows what is still allowed during the ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the afternoon ban on ערב פסח, a full meal is forbidden, but light snack foods are allowed.

steps.title: רבי יצחק would snack on vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי יצחק used to dip and eat vegetables on ערב פסח afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק would dip and eat vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what one sage actually did. He ate vegetables, which count as a light snack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real-life example of the rule from Step 9. Vegetables do not fill you up, so they do not ruin your appetite for the סדר. A sage's practice shows the rule is followed in real life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak would dip and eat vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real example of the snack rule stated in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vegetables count as an allowed light snack before the סדר.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports snacking: the waiter serves intestines
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the waiter dips intestines and serves them to the guests on ערב פסח, which supports the snack rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: The waiter dips intestines and puts them in front of the guests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the rule that light snacks are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תניא נמי הכי means 'a ברייתא also teaches this,' so it is support. The guests were the people signed up for the קרבן פסח. Small pieces of intestines were served as a snack to open their appetite, not to fill them up.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this way (a formula that brings support)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
the waiter dips the intestines
phrases.notes: Innards from animals slaughtered for the חג.

phrases.english: and places them before the guests.
phrases.notes: As a light snack to whet their appetite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the snack rule from Steps 9-10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that light snacking is allowed on ערב פסח afternoon.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing a waiter serving dipped intestines to the guests.

steps.title: A hint from a פסוק: prepare the ground first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that, while there is no full proof, there is a hint from ירמיה: 'Plow your field, and do not sow among thorns.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint to it, as it says: 'Plow for yourselves a plowed field, and do not sow among thorns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives a hint from a פסוק to support the idea of snacking first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a farmer prepares the soil before planting, a person 'prepares' his stomach with a small snack. Then he can eat the קרבן פסח and מצה at night with a good appetite. The ברייתא admits this is only a hint (זכר), not a real proof (ראיה).

keyTerms.meaning: there is no real proof for the matter
a hint or reminder for the matter (weaker than a proof)
plow for yourselves a plowed field (ירמיה ד:ג)

steps.whatToRemember: Before the סדר, a full meal is forbidden, but light snacks are allowed and even good. They 'prepare the ground' so you eat the מצה with appetite.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter, as it is said:
"Plow for yourselves a plowed field,
phrases.notes: This is from ירמיה ד:ג: first get the soil ready.

phrases.english: and do not sow among thorns."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding a hint from a פסוק for the snacking practice.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a light snack before the meal helps one eat more at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיה ד:ג, 'נירו לכם ניר ואל תזרעו אל קוצים,' brought as a hint only.

steps.title: רבא drank wine all day on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רבא drank wine all day on ערב פסח so he would have a bigger appetite for מצה at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא used to drink wine the whole day of ערב פסח, so that it would open his appetite and he would eat more מצה at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבא's practice on ערב פסח. It fits the same idea: do things in the day that help you eat more מצה at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא believed wine does not fill you up. Instead, it makes you hungrier. So drinking wine during the day is not against the ban. It actually helps the goal of eating מצה with appetite.

keyTerms.meaning: it will draw out his heart, meaning open his appetite

phrases.english: Rava would drink wine
the entire day of Passover eve,
phrases.notes: Even in the afternoon, during the ban.

phrases.english: so that it would whet his appetite
so he would eat more matza at night.
phrases.notes: The goal is eating מצה with appetite.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה שָׁתֵי חַמְרָא כּוּלֵּי מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִיסְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from food snacks to wine, which רבא drank to build appetite, the same goal as the snack hint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking wine on ערב פסח is allowed and even helpful, because wine increases appetite for מצה.

steps.title: רבא starts to bring a source that wine builds appetite
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how he knows wine opens the appetite, and begins to quote a משנה as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I know that wine opens the appetite? As we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא is getting ready to prove that wine makes you hungrier, and the actual משנה comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's practice in Step 13 depends on one claim: wine increases appetite and does not fill you up. Here he opens a proof for that claim with 'מנא אמינא לה' ('how do I know this?'). The word דתנן tells us the proof will be a משנה, which is quoted on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say it? (introduces a proof for one's own claim)

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: רבא now defends his own practice.

phrases.english: From where do I say it
that wine whets the appetite?
As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: The משנה is quoted on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דְּחַמְרָא מִיגְרָר גָּרֵיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a proof for the claim behind רבא's practice in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that wine increases appetite rather than filling a person up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה introduced with דתנן, quoted on the next amud.
